label: def:beta-decay-skein
title: Beta decay as a Skein crossing change on the Gröbner normal form
html:
Beta decay inserts the weak-force torus knot T_{3,5} at the converting quark of a nuclear Gröbner–Shirshov normal form \mathcal{N}(Z, N). The braid word is \beta_{T_{3,5}} = (\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5. It has 10 crossings. The operation concludes with re-reduction. The emitted electron is the word e^- = \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 (electron), whose closure is the Hopf link; the positron is e^+ = \sigma_0^{-1}\sigma_1^{-1}\sigma_0^{-1} (positron). Written in the generators \sigma_0, \sigma_1 of the electron word, the vertex is (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^5, and it carries the electron word as a braid factor:

  (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^5 = e^- \cdot \bigl(e^- \cdot (\sigma_0\sigma_1)^2\bigr) \quad\text{in } B_3 ,

so the 10 letters split into the 3 of e^- and a positive residue of 7.

A \beta^- transition inserts the T_{3,5} braid at the converting \mathfrak{d}-quark crossing of \mathcal{N}(Z, N), followed by re-reduction:

  \mathcal{N}(Z, N) \cdot \beta_{T_{3,5}}
  \xrightarrow{ \text{reduce}}
  \mathcal{N}(Z + 1,  N - 1)
  \sqcup
  e^-
  \sqcup
  K_{0_1}^{\sigma}.

A \beta^+ transition is the mirror operation. It inserts the conjugate T_{3,5}^{\sigma} braid with q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}:

  \mathcal{N}(Z, N) \cdot \beta_{T_{3,5}}^{\sigma}
  \xrightarrow{ \text{reduce}}
  \mathcal{N}(Z - 1,  N + 1)
  \sqcup
  e^+
  \sqcup
  K_{0_1}.
